key_insight: Adding water vapor, liquid water, and phase changes modifies inverse energy transfer in rotating stratified turbulence, producing moist PV-driven large-scale coherence and cloud-boundary-aligned updraft/downdraft structures.
engineering_relevance: This matters for geophysical flow and weather-model physics because moisture and phase transitions can change how energy cascades to large, coherent motions in rotating stratified environments.
method: Boussinesq dynamical core augmented with vapor, liquid water, and asymptotically fast cloud microphysics
Compared moist and dry regimes using Rossby number plus two Froude numbers (unsaturated and saturated)
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed inverse-energy-transfer behavior and statistical links between moist PV, phase boundaries, and coherent vertical motions, with reduced transfer rates relative to the dry case at fixed Rossby and dry Froude numbers.
watch_item: Results are based on an idealized model with asymptotically fast microphysics, so transfer rates and coherence patterns may differ in more complete atmospheric simulations.
paper_title: Inverse Transfer and Coherence in Rotating Stratified Flow with Clouds and Phase Transitions
